reason: E1 shows OCP drops sharply during loading and recovers during no-load, supporting the film rupture-repassivation concept and OCP monitoring. E2 describes passive film growth and suppression of anodic reaction on CoCrFeNiMoCu0.1, supporting repassivation capability. However, no cited evidence directly quantifies the balance between removal and repassivation kinetics, nor demonstrates that faster repassivation reduces overall degradation in a comparative test; these remain unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mechanical friction locally ruptures the passive oxide film on HEAs.
Ruptured film exposes bare metal which then rapidly repassivates.
Overall tribo-corrosion degradation is governed by the balance between wear-induced film removal and repassivation kinetics.
Faster repassivation minimizes the duration of corrosive attack, reducing overall degradation.
OCP fluctuations during sliding can monitor the passivation state within the wear track.
